title: George Nicholson and the Benny Carter influence
summary: A new tenor player in Tweed Beard's band, and how young altos like Stitt and Wardell Gray modeled themselves on Benny Carter.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Coleman Hawkins and the great saxophonists

blocks.x: Anyway, back to Tweed(?) Beard. We were working a little place out on Grand River, a little dance hall out there, a bar. And he had just hired a saxophone player from...was it Saginaw...anyway, one of those little towns up in Michigan -- and that was George Nicholson, a tenor player, his first time away from home. [LAUGHS HEARTILY] And he was playing good. He had Ben Webster on his mind, you know.

And this was during the period with Ben Webster, and all the alto players mostly had their minds on Charlie Parker... Like, Sonny Stitt hadn't heard Charlie Parker yet. He was playing strictly out of the Benny Carter bag, and Wardell was playing out of the Benny Carter bag, and Bernie Peacock -- they was all working out of Benny Carter's bag. And one period there when Benny Carter was out here, working at the Club Alabam, you could get him faintly on the radio late at night in Detroit -- get him faintly, boy. And we'd be staying up so we could hear that little bit of taste; get a little taste of Benny Carter! [LAUGHS HEARTILY] Oh boy!
